cases.sentence: В 1811-м году в Москве жил быстро вошедший в моду ___, огромный ростом, красавец, любезный, как француз и, как говорили все в Москве, врач необыкновенного искусства — Метивье.
cases.explain: «французский доктор» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: In 1811 there was living in Moscow a French doctor—Métivier—who had rapidly become the fashion. He was enormously tall, handsome, amiable as Frenchmen are, and was, as all Moscow said, an extraordinarily clever doctor. He was received in the best houses not merely as a doctor, but as an equal.

cases.sentence: В 1811-м году в Москве жил быстро вошедший в моду французский доктор, огромный ростом, красавец, любезный, как француз и, как говорили все в Москве, врач ___ — Метивье.
cases.explain: «необыкновенного искусства» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: In 1811 there was living in Moscow a French doctor—Métivier—who had rapidly become the fashion. He was enormously tall, handsome, amiable as Frenchmen are, and was, as all Moscow said, an extraordinarily clever doctor. He was received in the best houses not merely as a doctor, but as an equal.

cases.sentence: Случилось так, что в это имянинное утро ___ был в одном из своих самых дурных расположений духа.
cases.explain: «старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Métivier, who came in the morning with his felicitations, considered it proper in his quality of doctor de forcer la consigne,71 as he told Princess Márya, and went in to see the prince. It happened that on that morning of his name day the prince was in one of his worst moods. He had been going about the house all the morning finding fault with everyone and pretending not to understand what was said to him and not to be understood himself. Princess Márya well knew this mood of quiet absorbed querulousness, which generally culminated in a burst of rage, and she went about all that morning as though facing a cocked and loaded gun and awaited the inevitable explosion. Until the doctor’s arrival the morning had passed off safely. After admitting the doctor, Princess Márya sat down with a book in the drawing room near the door through which she could hear all that passed in the study.

cases.sentence: ___, Бонапартов раб, шпион, вон из моего дома — вон, я говорю!
cases.explain: «Французский шпион» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “You don’t understand?” shouted the prince, “but I do! French spy, slave of Bonaparte, spy, get out of my house! Be off, I tell you …” and he slammed the door.

cases.sentence: Метивье пожимая плечами подошел к mademoiselle Bourienne, прибежавшей на крик из ___.
cases.explain: «соседней комнаты» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Métivier, shrugging his shoulders, went up to Mademoiselle Bourienne who at the sound of shouting had run in from an adjoining room.

cases.sentence: После отъезда Метивье ___ позвал к себе дочь и вся сила его гнева обрушилась на нее.
cases.explain: «старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: After Métivier’s departure the old prince called his daughter in, and the whole weight of his wrath fell on her. She was to blame that a spy had been admitted. Had he not told her, yes, told her to make a list, and not to admit anyone who was not on that list? Then why was that scoundrel admitted? She was the cause of it all. With her, he said, he could not have a moment’s peace and could not die quietly.

cases.sentence: Гости — ___ Растопчин, князь Лопухин с своим племянником, генерал Чатров, старый, боевой товарищ князя, и из молодых Пьер и Борис Друбецкой — ждали его в гостиной.
cases.explain: «известный граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: At two o’clock the six chosen guests assembled for dinner. These guests—the famous Count Rostopchín, Prince Lopukhín with his nephew, General Chatróv an old war comrade of the prince’s, and of the younger generation Pierre and Borís Drubetskóy—awaited the prince in the drawing room.

cases.sentence: Дом князя был не то, что называется «свет», но это был такой ___, о котором хотя и не слышно было в городе, но в котором лестнее всего было быть принятым.
cases.explain: «маленький кружок» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The prince’s house did not belong to what is known as fashionable society, but his little circle—though not much talked about in town—was one it was more flattering to be received in than any other. Borís had realized this the week before when the commander in chief in his presence invited Rostopchín to dinner on St. Nikoláy’s Day, and Rostopchín had replied that he could not come:

cases.sentence: ___, собравшееся в старомодной, высокой, с старою мебелью, гостиной перед обедом, было похоже на собравшийся, торжественный совет судилища.
cases.explain: «Небольшое общество» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The small group that assembled before dinner in the lofty old-fashioned drawing room with its old furniture resembled the solemn gathering of a court of justice. All were silent or talked in low tones. Prince Nikoláy Andréevich came in serious and taciturn. Princess Márya seemed even quieter and more diffident than usual. The guests were reluctant to address her, feeling that she was in no mood for their conversation. Count Rostopchín alone kept the conversation going, now relating the latest town news, and now the latest political gossip.

cases.sentence: Небольшое общество, собравшееся в старомодной, высокой, с старою мебелью, гостиной перед обедом, было похоже на собравшийся, ___ судилища.
cases.explain: «торжественный совет» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: Граф Растопчин один держал нить разговора, рассказывая о последних то городских, то ___.
cases.explain: «политических новостях» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The small group that assembled before dinner in the lofty old-fashioned drawing room with its old furniture resembled the solemn gathering of a court of justice. All were silent or talked in low tones. Prince Nikoláy Andréevich came in serious and taciturn. Princess Márya seemed even quieter and more diffident than usual. The guests were reluctant to address her, feeling that she was in no mood for their conversation. Count Rostopchín alone kept the conversation going, now relating the latest town news, and now the latest political gossip.

cases.sentence: Лопухин и ___ изредка принимали участие в разговоре.
cases.explain: «старый генерал» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Lopukhín and the old general occasionally took part in the conversation. Prince Nikoláy Andréevich listened as a presiding judge receives a report, only now and then, silently or by a brief word, showing that he took heed of what was being reported to him. The tone of the conversation was such as indicated that no one approved of what was being done in the political world. Incidents were related evidently confirming the opinion that everything was going from bad to worse, but whether telling a story or giving an opinion the speaker always stopped, or was stopped, at the point beyond which his criticism might touch the sovereign himself.

cases.sentence: Князь Николай Андреич слушал, как ___ слушает доклад, который делают ему, только изредка молчанием или коротким словцом заявляя, что он принимает к сведению то, что ему докладывают.

cases.sentence: За обедом разговор зашел о последней политической новости, о захвате Наполеоном владений герцога Ольденбургского и о русской враждебной Наполеону ноте, посланной ко всем ___.
cases.explain: «европейским дворам» — after the preposition «о», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: At dinner the talk turned on the latest political news: Napoleon’s seizure of the Duke of Oldenburg’s territory, and the Russian Note, hostile to Napoleon, which had been sent to all the European courts.

cases.sentence: — Предложили ___ заместо Ольденбургского герцогства, — сказал князь Николай Андреич.
cases.explain: «другие владения» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Other territories have been offered in exchange for the Duchy of Oldenburg,” said Prince Nikoláy Andréevich. “He shifts the Dukes about as I might move my serfs from Bald Hills to Boguchárovo or my Ryazán estates.”

cases.sentence: — Предложили другие владения заместо ___, — сказал князь Николай Андреич.
cases.explain: «Ольденбургского герцогства» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Other territories have been offered in exchange for the Duchy of Oldenburg,” said Prince Nikoláy Andréevich. “He shifts the Dukes about as I might move my serfs from Bald Hills to Boguchárovo or my Ryazán estates.”

cases.sentence: Князь Николай Андреич посмотрел на ___ так, как будто он хотел бы ему сказать кое-что на это, но раздумал, считая его слишком для того молодым.
cases.explain: «молодого человека» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “The Duke of Oldenburg bears his misfortunes with admirable strength of character and resignation,” remarked Borís, joining in respectfully. He said this because on his journey from Petersburg he had had the honor of being presented to the Duke. Prince Nikoláy Andréevich glanced at the young man as if about to say something in reply, but changed his mind, evidently considering him too young.

cases.sentence: — Mon cher, avec nos 500 mille hommes de troupes, il serait facile d’avoir un beau style,[524] — Мой милый, с 500 тысячами войска было бы легко иметь ___, — сказал граф Растопчин.
cases.explain: «хороший слог» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “My dear fellow, with our five hundred thousand troops it should be easy to have a good style,” returned Count Rostopchín. Pierre now understood the count’s dissatisfaction with the wording of the Note.

cases.sentence: — Кажется, писак довольно развелось, — сказал ___: — там в Петербурге всё пишут, не только ноты, — новые законы всё пишут.
cases.explain: «старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “One would have thought quill drivers enough had sprung up,” remarked the old prince. “There in Petersburg they are always writing—not notes only but even new laws. My Andrúsha there has written a whole volume of laws for Russia. Nowadays they are always writing!” and he laughed unnaturally.

cases.sentence: — Кажется, писак довольно развелось, — сказал старый князь: — там в Петербурге всё пишут, не только ноты, — ___ всё пишут.
cases.explain: «новые законы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Разговор замолк на минуту; ___ прокашливаньем обратил на себя внимание.
cases.explain: «старый генерал» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: There was a momentary pause in the conversation; the old general cleared his throat to draw attention.

cases.sentence: — Изволили слышать о ___ на смотру в Петербурге?
cases.explain: «последнем событии» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Did you hear of the last event at the review in Petersburg? The figure cut by the new French ambassador.”

cases.sentence: И он рассказал весь свой разговор с ___ и причины, почему он убедился, что Метивье шпион.
cases.explain: «французским доктором» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Impudent fellows!” said the prince. “You know Métivier? I turned him out of my house this morning. He was here; they admitted him in spite of my request that they should let no one in,” he went on, glancing angrily at his daughter. And he narrated his whole conversation with the French doctor and the reasons that convinced him that Métivier was a spy. Though these reasons were very insufficient and obscure, no one made any rejoinder.

cases.sentence: Гости встали с своих мест, поздравляя ___.
cases.explain: «старого князя» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: After the roast, champagne was served. The guests rose to congratulate the old prince. Princess Márya, too, went round to him.

cases.sentence: Всё выражение его лица говорило ей, что ___ им не забыт, что решенье его осталось в прежней силе, и что только благодаря присутствию гостей он не говорит ей этого теперь.
cases.explain: «утренний разговор» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: He gave her a cold, angry look and offered her his wrinkled, clean-shaven cheek to kiss. The whole expression of his face told her that he had not forgotten the morning’s talk, that his decision remained in force, and only the presence of visitors hindered his speaking of it to her now.

cases.sentence: Всё выражение его лица говорило ей, что утренний разговор им не забыт, что решенье его осталось в ___, и что только благодаря присутствию гостей он не говорит ей этого теперь.

The whole expression of his face told her that he had not forgotten the morning’s talk, that his decision remained in force, and only the presence of visitors hindered his speaking of it to her now.

cases.sentence: Князь Николай Андреич более оживился и высказал свой образ мыслей насчет ___.
cases.explain: «предстоящей войны» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Prince Nikoláy Andréevich grew more animated and expressed his views on the impending war.

cases.sentence: Он сказал, что войны наши с Бонапартом до тех пор будут несчастливы, пока мы будем искать союзов с немцами и будем соваться в ___, в которые нас втянул Тильзитский мир.
cases.explain: «Европейские дела» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: He said that our wars with Bonaparte would be disastrous so long as we sought alliances with the Germans and thrust ourselves into European affairs, into which we had been drawn by the Peace of Tilsit. “We ought not to fight either for or against Austria. Our political interests are all in the East, and in regard to Bonaparte the only thing is to have an armed frontier and a firm policy, and he will never dare to cross the Russian frontier, as was the case in 1807!”

cases.sentence: Он сказал, что войны наши с Бонапартом до тех пор будут несчастливы, пока мы будем искать союзов с немцами и будем соваться в Европейские дела, в которые нас втянул ___.
cases.explain: «Тильзитский мир» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: He said that our wars with Bonaparte would be disastrous so long as we sought alliances with the Germans and thrust ourselves into European affairs, into which we had been drawn by the Peace of Tilsit. “We ought not to fight either for or against Austria. Our political interests are all in the East, and in regard to Bonaparte the only thing is to have an armed frontier and a firm policy, and he will never dare to cross the Russian frontier, as was the case in 1807!”

cases.sentence: ___ с улыбкой на лице смотрел на Растопчина и одобрительно покачивал головой.
cases.explain: «Старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: All were silent. The old prince looked at Rostopchín with a smile and wagged his head approvingly.

cases.sentence: — Ну, прощайте, ваше сиятельство, не хворайте, — сказал Растопчин, с свойственными ему ___ поднимаясь и протягивая руку князю.
cases.explain: «быстрыми движениями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Well, goodbye, your excellency, keep well!” said Rostopchín, getting up with characteristic briskness and holding out his hand to the prince.

cases.sentence: — сказал ___, удерживая его за руку и подставляя ему для поцелуя щеку.
cases.explain: «старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Goodbye, my dear fellow. … His words are music, I never tire of hearing him!” said the old prince, keeping hold of the hand and offering his cheek to be kissed. Following Rostopchín’s example the others also rose.
